title: The canonical Tor coefficient map in free-resolution coordinates
statement:
Let $R\to A\xrightarrow{g}B$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings with their composite $R\to B$, and $M$ an $R$-module. Let $P_\bullet\to M$ be an exact augmented free $R$-resolution in degrees $j\geq0$, with freeness as in [def-weil-pbc-free-module], extended by zero in negative degrees. Put $C=P_\bullet\otimes_R A$ and $D=P_\bullet\otimes_R B$, without augmentations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. Let $\iota_{A,n}:\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,A)\to H_n(C)$ and $\iota_{B,n}:\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,B)\to H_n(D)$ be the canonical resolution-computation isomorphisms for Tor [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. By [lem-trf-tor-resolution-coefficient-actions], for the coefficient actions of [def-trf-tor-coefficient-module] and the actions on homology by multiplication in the coefficient factor, $\iota_{A,n}$ is $A$-linear, $\iota_{B,n}$ is $B$-linear, and the $A$-action on $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,B)$ is the restriction of its $B$-action along $g$; so $\iota_{A,n}\otimes_A1_B$ and the map $c_n$ below are well defined. The formulas $\phi_j(p\otimes a)=p\otimes g(a)$ define an $A$-linear chain map $\phi:C\to\operatorname{Res}_gD$, where $\operatorname{Res}_g$ means restriction of scalars along $g$. For every $n\geq0$ let $h_n:H_n(C)\to H_n(D)$ be its induced map and let
$$\alpha_n:H_n(C)\otimes_A B\to H_n(D),\qquad [z]\otimes b\mapsto b\cdot h_n([z])$$
be its $B$-linear tensor extension. Let $c_n$ be the canonical coefficient-base-change map, namely the $B$-linear extension of the coefficient map $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,g)$, so $c_n(t\otimes b)=b\cdot\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,g)(t)$. Then
$$\iota_{B,n}\circ c_n=\alpha_n\circ(\iota_{A,n}\otimes_A1_B).$$
More explicitly, for every cycle $z=\sum_i p_i\otimes a_i\in C_n$ and $b\in B$ both sides send $\iota_{A,n}^{-1}([z])\otimes b$ to $[\sum_i p_i\otimes g(a_i)b]$. This identity holds for every choice of free resolution and requires no flatness; no invertibility of $c_n$ or $\alpha_n$ is asserted.

proof.text: Use the existing tensoringRight natural transformation for the coefficient homomorphism. Its component sends p tensor a to p tensor g(a) definitionally. Tensor induction proves that it commutes with coefficient multiplication by a: the pure-tensor case is map_mul and the zero and sum cases are additivity. The natural transformation already supplies the chain compatibility.

proof.text: The supplied ProjectiveResolution already provides projective terms; no separate conversion from freeness is needed. Apply ProjectiveResolution.leftDerived_app_eq, clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift], to the coefficient homomorphism. Compose with the B-resolution isomorphism and cancel its inverse. Tor'_obj_map and evaluation give iota_B Tor(M,g)(t) = H(phi) iota_A(t).

proof.text: First prove the transported homology action formula by applying [lem-trf-tor-resolution-coefficient-actions] to the inverse image of a homology class under iota, then using linearity and the inverse identities. The restriction and scalar-associativity clauses of that lemma provide the A-action and the A/B scalar tower on coefficient-B Tor. LinearMap.liftBaseChange extends the existing A-linear coefficient map to c, with c(b tensor t)=b Tor(M,g)(t). Define alpha = iota_B composed with c composed with the B-base-change of iota_A inverse. These are explicit linear maps. The naturality equality of Step 2 and coefficient linearity give alpha(b tensor x)=b H(phi)(x).

Tensor extensionality proves the comparison square from the two pure-tensor formulas and Step 2. Any other pair satisfying those formulas equals (c,alpha) by tensor extensionality, proving uniqueness. Given z=sum p_i tensor a_i and b, let mu be the chain endomorphism multiplying the B factor by b, and let w be the image of z under cyclesMap(phi composed with mu). The cyclesMap_i identity, additivity, and the pure-tensor formulas give iCycles(w)=sum p_i tensor (g(a_i)b), using commutativity. Homology-pi naturality and homologyMap_comp identify its class with H(mu)(H(phi)([z])). The transported action formula identifies that with b H(phi)([z]). The formulas for c and alpha now give both asserted values. This uses no exactness after tensoring, flatness or invertibility of the extensions.
